_readme: Shared cross-language corpus for the display-link safety rule.
SPEC ANCHOR: spec/API.md §Data Resource -> 'Display-link safety'. That block's
rule-class table is the source of every case here; each case carries a `rule` key
naming the row it derives from (Scheme / Authority / Characters / Shape / Length).
A case that cannot cite a row does not belong in this file.
The rule is hand-maintained in three places, and nothing but this corpus makes a
one-sided edit fail:
1. src/api/schemas/common.py SAFE_DISPLAY_URL_PATTERN / SAFE_PROJECT_ID_PATTERN,
compiled by Python `re` and used by sanitize_display_url / sanitize_project_id
at the READ boundary (spec: 'On read, GET /spoke/common/peripheral-links
coerces one to ""').
2. The same constants handed to pydantic Field(pattern=...) at the WRITE boundary
(spec: 'On write, PATCH /admin/peripherals/{datahub,langfuse} rejects a
violating value with 422'), compiled by pydantic's Rust regex engine, NOT by
Python `re`.
3. src/frontend/lib/safe-url.ts, compiled by the JavaScript engine (spec:
FRONTEND_BASIC.md §Shell -- 'Both peripheral values are re-checked in the
client against the display-link safety rule ... The client check is not
redundant with the API's: it also covers the env-sourced values').
Asserted by BOTH:
- tests/unit/api/schemas/test_safe_url_corpus.py  (engines 1 and 2)
- src/frontend/lib/safe-url.test.ts               (engine 3)
Add a case here, not to one language's test file. `accept` and `reject` must hold
identically in every engine.
SHAPE IS NOT AN ANTI-SPOOFING RULE. The spec says so outright: a path, query, or
fragment must be introduced by `/`, and 'This is a grammar constraint, not an
anti-spoofing rule.' The corpus shows both sides -- `https://evil.com?x=1` is
rejected and `https://evil.com/?x=1` is accepted, and the effective host is
`evil.com` either way. Do not relabel these as spoofing defences; the guard does
not have that property and only Authority (userinfo) and Characters (bidi) do.
`engine_divergence` is intentionally empty: every case here is answered the same
way by all three engines. The bucket is kept as a documented home for a future
disagreement -- record it with each side's answer, a `why`, and a `remediation`,
rather than deleting the case or silently pinning one side. Both suites assert the
bucket is empty, so adding an entry is a deliberate, visible act.
U+FEFF and U+0085 are Characters cases needing both classes to name them
explicitly: Python `\s` follows the Unicode White_Space property (includes NEL,
excludes ZWNBSP) and ECMAScript `\s` follows the WhiteSpace production (the exact
inverse). The spec's 'No whitespace' is only satisfied under the union of the two
definitions, which is what both classes now encode.
Invisible characters are stored as \uXXXX escapes on purpose: a literal one would
be unreviewable in a diff.
BRACKETED IPv6 LITERALS ARE REJECTED, and the spec states that as an outcome rather
than an accident: 'The Authority rule admits a hostname plus an optional numeric port
and nothing else, so a bracketed IPv6 literal (http://[::1]:8080) is rejected. For a
display link that costs only the deep link; for gms_url it means an IPv6-only GMS must
be addressed by hostname.' The cases live here rather than in one language's test file
because the spec also says widening the authority is 'a coordinated change rather than
a one-line edit ... both move together or not at all'.

_rule_classes.Scheme: Lowercase http:// or https://, or "" meaning unset. Lowercasing is a strictness choice for an operator-entered config field, not a safety property; the host itself stays case-insensitive.
_rule_classes.Authority: A host plus an optional numeric port and nothing else. Userinfo is rejected.
_rule_classes.Characters: No whitespace, no C0 control characters, and no unicode bidi-override characters anywhere in the value.
_rule_classes.Shape: A path, query, or fragment must be introduced by `/`. A grammar constraint, NOT an anti-spoofing rule.
_rule_classes.Length: Bounded -- 512 for a URL, 256 for project_id, which is further restricted to an alphanumeric slug.
_rule_classes.Slug: The project_id sub-rule of the Length row: an alphanumeric slug. Split out from Length so that the length BOUND (512 / 256) is exercised by its own boundary cases rather than being reported as covered by slug-grammar cases.

accept.label: slash-introduced query, host still evil.com (grammar, not anti-spoofing)
slash-introduced fragment, host still evil.com (grammar, not anti-spoofing)

reject.label: uppercase scheme (strictness choice, not a safety property)
bracketed IPv6 literal with a port
bracketed IPv6 literal without a port
fragment not introduced by a slash (grammar)
query not introduced by a slash (grammar)
trailing LF after an otherwise valid URL
OGHAM SPACE MARK in the host
ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE (BOM) in the host
